description: Parameters needed to the corresponding task specification in eTaSL

from-force_control_task_lib-version-1.0..description:
Library force_control_task_lib version 1.0.3.
 Set to true to indicate that task specification comes from the library above. 
 Library description: Library with eTaSL task specifications for force control tasks for Crospi
Authors: Santiago Iregui (KU Leuven), Erwin Aertbeliën (KU Leuven), Federico Ulloa (KU Leuven)

file_path.description: File path of the corresponding task specification

parameters.description: List of parameters needed to define an instance of the task specification

FT_sensor_frame.description: Name of the robot frame (from the robot model) of the force/torque sensor. The measured wrench of the input channel is expressed in this frame, with its origin as reference point

max_angular_velocity.description: Maximum absolute angular velocity [rad/s] of the control frame around each of its axes

K_F.description: Diagonal elements [N/m] of the translational stiffness, as [x,y,z] along the axes of the control frame, used as model of the force control: the velocity along each axis is K_force*(desired force - measured force)/K_F. Lower values make the robot faster and more compliant along that axis, higher values slower and stiffer. The compliant axes should have a low value so that the robot follows the object (e.g. the arc of a door) with a small force

axis.description: Axis of the control frame (task_frame*tf_2_insframe) along which the robot pushes or pulls. The direction is given by the sign of force. The distance travelled is measured along it

K_force.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the force control constraints along x, y and z (inverse of their time constant)

tf_2_insframe.description: Pose of the control frame w.r.t. task_frame, as [x,y,z,qx,qy,qz,qw] (position in m, unit quaternion with the real part qw last), expressed in task_frame. The axis of the motion, the forces and the torques are expressed in this frame, and the torques are w.r.t. its origin (e.g. the center of the handle that is grasped). Use it when the gripper is not aligned with the direction of the motion (e.g. a tool tilted downwards that pulls horizontally). The default is the identity

force.description: Desired force [N] exerted by the robot on the environment along axis, in the control frame. Its sign is the direction of the motion: the robot moves along +axis if it is positive (it pushes in the direction +axis), along -axis if it is negative (it pulls). In free space the velocity along the axis is K_force*force/K_F (limited by maxvel); in contact the robot stops moving when the measured force reaches this value, so a force larger than the resisting force (friction of a drawer or door) is needed to move it

maxvel.description: Maximum absolute velocity [m/s] of the control frame along each of its axes

force_threshold.description: Dead zone [N] applied to each force component of the measured wrench (in FT_sensor_frame): components with an absolute value below it are set to zero and larger ones are reduced by it. 0 disables the dead zone

contact_force.description: Contact threshold [N] for a guarded motion: the task finishes when the force exerted by the robot along axis in the direction of the motion exceeds this value (after time_delay). 0 disables this monitor (the task then only finishes by distance or max_time). It should be smaller than the absolute value of force, otherwise the robot stops before reaching it

distance.description: Distance [m] travelled along axis (integral of the velocity along the axis of the control frame, see the description of the task) after which the task finishes. Its sign is ignored. It acts as a maximum when contact_force is used

weight_torque.description: Weight [-] of the torque control constraints relative to the other constraints of the same priority. Only matters when the constraints conflict

K_torque.description: Feedback gain [1/s] of the torque control constraints around x, y and z (inverse of their time constant)

torque_threshold.description: Dead zone [Nm] applied to each torque component of the measured wrench (in FT_sensor_frame). 0 disables the dead zone

max_time.description: Maximum duration [s] of the task: it finishes when this time has elapsed. 0 disables this monitor

K_T.description: Diagonal elements [Nm/rad] of the rotational stiffness, as [x,y,z] around the axes of the control frame, used as model of the torque control: the angular velocity around each axis is K_torque*(0 - measured torque)/K_T, i.e. the robot rotates with the object (e.g. a door handle that turns) with a small torque. Lower values make the robot rotate faster for the same torque

wrench_input_channel.description: Name of the input channel (type wrench) from which the measured wrench of the force/torque sensor is read: the channel fed directly by the robot driver/simulator (name_expr_cartesian_wrench of the MuJoCo simulator) or the varname of an input handler that provides it. The wrench is the wrench exerted by the end effector on the environment

task_frame.description: Name of the robot frame (from the robot model) that is controlled, e.g. the tool center point. The control frame is defined w.r.t. this frame by tf_2_insframe

weight_max_velocity.description: Weight [-] of the constraints that limit the velocities (higher priority than the force and torque control)

weight_force.description: Weight [-] of the force control constraints relative to the other constraints of the same priority. Only matters when the constraints conflict

time_delay.description: Time [s] after the start of the task during which the contact monitor (contact_force) is disabled, to ignore forces present at the beginning

is-move_compliant.description:
Task Specification: move_compliant.etasl.lua
Set to true to indicate that the task uses the task specification mentioned above. 
 Task description:  Task to implement task frame formalism, A task frame here is defined between two frame where tf typically corresponds to the 
end effector and wrt to the world.  There is a list of controllers and a list of setpoints. The controller specifies the type (force/velocity/tracking) and direction x,y or z
